_doc: Valori trascritti a mano dai capitoli di USDA ARS Agriculture Handbook 66 (2016) che il parser automatico non aggancia (capitoli multi-prodotto, tabelle di respirazione nei capitoli) o dove la Tab. 1 del PDF contiene refusi (es. Radicchio 8/1310/2311). 'quote' = frase o dati della fonte. Respirazione: classe di Kader a 5 °C; se il capitolo non riporta 5 °C si interpola in modo esponenziale (media geometrica tra 0 e 10 °C), come indicato in 'resp_basis'. Pagine = numerazione del PDF.

rosmarino_rosemary.quote: rosemary, sage, and thyme will last for 2 to 3 weeks [at 0 °C]; These perennial herbs are not chilling sensitive; Ethylene production is low, but sensitivity is high.

salvia_sage.quote: rosemary, sage, and thyme will last for 2 to 3 weeks; not chilling sensitive; Ethylene production is low, but sensitivity is high. Tab. 1: Sage ethylene 'very low'.

timo_thyme.quote: rosemary, sage, and thyme will last for 2 to 3 weeks; not chilling sensitive; Ethylene production is low, but sensitivity is high.

menta_mint.quote: Chives and mint can be stored for 2 to 3 weeks at 0 °C with 95 to 100% RH; not chilling sensitive; Ethylene production is low, but sensitivity is high.

symptoms.en: Browning or blackening of the leaves

basilico_basil.quote: Basil should be stored at 12 °C and 95 to 100% RH ... quality can be maintained for 2 weeks; Basil is susceptible to chilling injury if stored below 12 °C ... browning or blackening of the leaves; Annual herbs produce very little ethylene, but are highly susceptible to ethylene exposure.

rucola_arugula.quote: Salad greens should be stored at 0 to 2 °C with 95 to 100% RH. Rocket salad typically lasts 7 to 10 days; not sensitive to chilling; very low ethylene production but highly sensitive to ethylene exposure.

valerianella_corn_salad.quote: Salad greens should be stored at 0 to 2 °C with 95 to 100% RH ... other leafy greens 10 to 14 days; not sensitive to chilling; highly sensitive to ethylene.

tartufo_nero_black_truffle.quote: Truffles can be kept in good condition for 20 to 30 days at 0 ºC with 90 to 95% RH; not chilling sensitive; produce only very low amounts of ethylene and are not sensitive to ethylene exposure.
tartufo_nero_black_truffle.quote_storage: Truffles can be kept in good condition for 20 to 30 days at 0 ºC (32 °F) with 90 to 95% RH.

radicchio_radicchio.resp_basis: capitolo: 6 °C 10-16 mg CO2/kg·h (la Tab. 1 del PDF riporta 1310/2311, refuso)
radicchio_radicchio.quote: Exposure to 10 µL L-1 ethylene for 6 days at 7.5 °C ... increased leaf browning, decay, and pigmentation of midribs.

finocchio_fennel.resp_basis: capitolo: 2 °C 18-20 mg CO2/kg·h (Tab. 1 del PDF: 196, refuso)
finocchio_fennel.quote: No data exist on sensitivity to ethylene.

bietola_da_coste_swiss_chard.quote: Ethylene production is very low ... Sensitivity, however, is very high. Exposure results in yellowing and senescence.

carota_carrot.quote: exposure to ethylene (~0.2 µL L-1) induces development of the bitter compound isocoumarin ... should not be exposed to ethylene in storage.

pastinaca_parsnip.quote: Exposure to low levels of ethylene in cold storage causes bitterness.

melanzana_eggplant.quote: Eggplant fruit have a moderate to high sensitivity to ethylene exposure.

cicoria_da_cespo_chicory.quote: Production is very low, but exposure can result in leaf yellowing.

cicoria_da_taglio_cutting_chicory.quote: Production is very low, but exposure can result in leaf yellowing.

arancia_orange.quote: ethylene stimulates decay, such as anthracnose and stem-end rot ... Ethylene also increases respiration in citrus.

fico_fig.quote: Figs are climacteric fruit and are slightly sensitive to ethylene action on stimulating softening and decay severity.
fico_fig.quote_storage: Store at -1 to 0 ºC (30 to 32 ºF) with 90 to 95% RH.

mela_apple.quote: The timing of the climacteric and ripening of apple fruit is advanced by exposure to ethylene.

susina_plum.quote: for slow-ripening cultivars ... application of 100 µL L-1 for at least 24 h at 20 °C is needed for faster and more uniform ripening.

symptoms.it: La maggior parte delle varietà subisce danni da freddo se conservata a 5 °C (disfacimento interno); meglio 0 °C.
symptoms.en: Most cultivars suffer chilling injury when stored at 5 °C (internal breakdown); 0 °C is better.

susina_plum.quote_chill: Most plum and fresh prune cultivars are susceptible to chilling injury when stored at 5 °C (41 °F).

mango_mango.quote: Ethylene induces faster and more uniform softening.

melone_melon.quote: Netted melons have a moderate rate of respiration (Kader 1992).

pera_pear.quote: Ethylene production rates are low at harvest ... The magnitude of ethylene production at the climacteric-like peak is 10 to 20 mL kg-1 h-1 for 'd'Anjou', 40 to 80 for 'Bosc' (pere in maturazione a 20 °C).
pera_pear.quote_chill: Most pears in the Pacific Northwest are stored at -1 °C (30 °F) with RH of 90 to 94%

nespola_loquat.quote: Loquat fruit produce relatively low amounts of ethylene and are not particularly sensitive to ethylene exposure after harvest.
nespola_loquat.quote_storage: 0 to 5 °C (32 to 41 °F) with >90% RH ... 3 to 4 weeks at 0 °C

symptoms.it: Molte varietà di media e tarda stagione: imbrunimento e disfacimento interno della polpa, più rapidi tra 2 e 7 °C che a 0 °C.
symptoms.en: Most mid- and late-season cultivars: internal browning and breakdown, faster and more intense at 2-7 °C than at 0 °C or below.

pesca_peach.quote_chill: Chilling injury develops faster and more intensely in fruit stored at 2 to 7 °C (36 to 45 °F) than in those stored at 0 °C (32 °F) or below.

symptoms.it: Alcune varietà di media e tarda stagione: imbrunimento e disfacimento interno della polpa, più rapidi tra 2 e 8 °C che a 0 °C.
symptoms.en: Some mid- and late-season cultivars: internal browning and breakdown, faster and more intense between 2 and 8 °C than at 0 °C.

pesca_noce_nectarine.quote_chill: Chilling injury symptoms develop faster and more intensely when fruit are stored between about 2 and 8 °C (36 and 46 °F) than in those stored at 0 °C (32 °F) or below.

symptoms.it: Nelle varietà sensibili: polpa gelatinosa e imbrunita e perdita di sapore, più rapide a 5 °C che a 0 °C.
symptoms.en: In sensitive cultivars: gel breakdown, flesh browning and loss of flavour, faster at 5 °C than at 0 °C.

albicocca_apricot.quote_chill: Chilling-sensitive cultivars develop and express chilling injury symptoms (gel breakdown, flesh browning, and loss of flavor) more rapidly at 5 °C than at 0 °C.
albicocca_apricot.quote_freezing: The highest freezing point is -1.0 ºC

symptoms.it: Dipende dalla varietà: i cachi non astringenti tipo Fuyu tra 5 e 15 °C imbruniscono nella polpa e si ammorbidiscono; il tipo Hachiya non è sensibile.
symptoms.en: Depends on the cultivar: non-astringent Fuyu-type persimmons develop flesh browning and softening between 5 and 15 °C; Hachiya is not chilling sensitive.

cachi_persimmon.quote_storage: The optimum temperature for storing persimmons is 0±1 °C ... RH should be maintained at 90 to 95%. Postharvest life ... in ethylene-free air is 3 mo
cachi_persimmon.quote_chill: 'Hachiya' is not chilling sensitive while 'Fuyu' and similar nonastringent cultivars are sensitive at temperatures between 5 ºC and 15 ºC
cachi_persimmon.quote_eth: 0.1 to 0.5 µL kg-1 h-1 at 20 °C ... They are very sensitive to ethylene.

pisello_pea.quote_chill: Peas are not sensitive to low temperature
pisello_pea.quote_eth: <0.1 μL kg-1 h-1 at 20 °C ... moderately sensitive to ethylene after harvest

cavolo_nero_black_kale.resp_basis: dati per lo spinacio (il capitolo non ne ha altri): 5 °C 32-58 mg CO2/kg·h
cavolo_nero_black_kale.quote_storage: Greens should be stored near 0 °C (32 °F) with 95 to 98% RH.

cima_di_rapa_turnip_greens.resp_basis: dati per lo spinacio (il capitolo non ne ha altri): 5 °C 32-58 mg CO2/kg·h
cima_di_rapa_turnip_greens.quote_storage: Greens should be stored near 0 °C (32 °F) with 95 to 98% RH.

topinambur_jerusalem_artichoke.quote_storage: Tubers can be stored for 6 to 12 mo at 0 to 2 °C (32 to 34 °F) and 90 to 95% RH.
topinambur_jerusalem_artichoke.quote_chill: Tubers can withstand low temperatures without damage but freeze at -2.2 °C
topinambur_jerusalem_artichoke.quote_eth: Tubers are not sensitive to ethylene.

mela_cotogna_quince.quote_storage: Optimum storage temperature is -0.5 °C to 0 °C (31 to 32 °F) with about 90% RH. Storage life in air at -0.5 °C (31 °F) is 2 to 3 mo

symptoms.it: Sotto i 5 °C (in alcune varietà sotto i 10 °C): buccia butterata, bronzata e con macchie scure, più marciumi.
symptoms.en: Below 5 °C (below 10 °C in some cultivars): pitting, bronzing and dark spots on the peel, and more decay.

fico_d_india_prickly_pear.quote_storage: fruit can be kept for 2 to 5 weeks at 5 to 8 °C (41 to 46 °F) with 90 to 95% RH
fico_d_india_prickly_pear.quote_chill: especially chilling sensitive when stored at <5 °C (41 °F), but chilling injury may occur in some varieties at <10 °C
fico_d_india_prickly_pear.quote_eth: about 0.2 µL kg-1 h-1 at 20 °C (68 °F). They are not sensitive to ethylene exposure.

fungo_porcino_porcini_mushroom.quote_storage: Mushrooms can be held for 7 to 9 days upon rapid cooling and storing at 0 to 1 °C (32 to 34 °F) with 95% RH.
fungo_porcino_porcini_mushroom.quote_eth: Since ethylene causes browning of mushroom caps, they should be kept separate from ethylene-producing fruits and vegetables.

fungo_ovolo_caesars_mushroom.quote_storage: Mushrooms can be held for 7 to 9 days upon rapid cooling and storing at 0 to 1 °C (32 to 34 °F) with 95% RH.
fungo_ovolo_caesars_mushroom.quote_eth: Since ethylene causes browning of mushroom caps, they should be kept separate from ethylene-producing fruits and vegetables.

symptoms.it: La varietà Hayward può subire danni vicino a 0 °C: anello di polpa granulosa e acquosa all'apice, puntinature e macchie scure sulla buccia.
symptoms.en: Hayward can be injured near 0 °C: a ring of granular, water-soaked tissue at the stylar end, pitting and dark scald-like skin.

kiwi_kiwifruit.quote_chill: 'Hayward' are chilling sensitive at temperatures near 0 °C
kiwi_kiwifruit.quote_eth: Kiwifruit in storage are extremely sensitive to the presence of ethylene

symptoms.it: Sotto i 7 °C: buccia butterata, zone acquose, marciumi e scurimento della cavità dei semi.
symptoms.en: Below 7 °C: surface pitting, water-soaked areas, decay and seed-cavity discoloration.

peperoncino_chili_pepper.quote_storage: Fresh peppers can be kept for 2 to 3 weeks at 7 °C (45 °F) with 90 to 95% RH.
peperoncino_chili_pepper.quote_chill: Peppers are sensitive to chilling injury when stored below 7 °C
peperoncino_chili_pepper.quote_eth: 0.1 and 0.2 µL kg-1 h-1 at 10 and 20 °C

broccolo_broccoli.quote_storage: 2 to 3 weeks at 0 ºC (32 ºF) with 98 to 100% RH
broccolo_broccoli.quote_eth: <0.1 µL kg-1 h-1 at 20 ºC ... extremely sensitive to ethylene

sedano_rapa_celeriac.quote_eth: celeriac may be slightly sensitive to ethylene. Therefore, celeriac should not be stored with other fruit or vegetables that produce high levels of ethylene.

scarola_escarole.quote_eth: Production is very low, but exposure can result in leaf yellowing.

symptoms.it: A 5 °C o meno: butteratura della buccia.

pompelmo_grapefruit.quote_chill: Chilling injury can occur with low-temperature storage, typically 5 °C (41 °F) or below.

lime_lime.quote_storage: Limes should be cooled and stored at 10 °C (50 °F) with 95% RH.

ananas_pineapple.quote_storage: Temperatures of 7 to 12 °C ... RH of 85 to 95%

papaya_papaya.quote_storage: Store at 7 to 13 °C (45 to 55 °F) with 90 to 95% RH.
papaya_papaya.quote_eth: Ethylene rates in ripening fruit are 6 to 10 μL kg-1 h-1

mandarino_mandarin.quote_storage: Mandarin are stored at 5 to 8 °C (41 to 46 °F) with 95% RH for periods up to 4 weeks. Chilling injury can occur in storage if temperatures fall below 5 °C

indivia_riccia_curly_endive.quote_eth: Production is very low, but exposure can result in leaf yellowing.

clementine_clementine.quote_storage: Mandarin are stored at 5 to 8 °C (41 to 46 °F) with 95% RH for periods up to 4 weeks. Chilling injury can occur in storage if temperatures fall below 5 °C

patata_potato.quote_storage: Tubers for fresh consumption are stored at 7 to 10 °C (45 to 50 °F) ... Maintaining 95 to 99% RH is required at all times ... Storage at 0 to 2 °C (32 to 36 °F) increases the risk of freezing or chilling injury.

fava_broad_bean.chapter: Table 1 Compatible fresh fruits and vegetables (Beans, fava, lima: gruppo 1A)

uva_table_grape.quote_freezing: The highest freezing point for berries is -3.0 ºC
